normalisation_note: Compact authored records were schema-normalised by materialising IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS from their existing known-failure and contrary-evidence text. No property ID, status, source assignment, denominator or judgement changed.

measurement_system_model.requirement: State the action, consumer, consequence asymmetry, horizon and smallest difference that could alter action.
Define the property, unit of analysis, operating conditions, admissible interpretation and non-equivalent states.
Identify standards, reference methods, bridge samples, domain authority or triangulation; distinguish traceability from fitness.
Define population, frame, selection, missingness, censoring, destructive measurement and measurement-induced contamination.
Separate bias, repeatability, reproducibility, operator/instrument/environment/evaluator effects and interactions.
Demonstrate resolution/sensitivity/specificity and uncertainty relative to the decision margin, not a universal percentage.
Fix threshold, guard band, loss or classification rule; distinguish conformance, statistical control and practical importance.
Bind results to data, preprocessing, exclusions, evaluator, reference, threshold and software versions.
Use check standards, repeated anchors, proficiency/bridge studies and change records to detect evaluator/reference drift.
Block metric governance when decision-relevant states cannot be discriminated; use a cheaper authoritative deterministic discriminator when it already settles the decision.

measurement_diagnostic_classes.meaning: The measurement contract is stable and independently fit; the candidate/process differs in the decision-relevant property.
Instrument, fixture, operator, environment, algorithm or repeatability/reproducibility failure explains the observation.
The operationalised metric does not preserve the intended property or decision-relevant distinctions.
Frame, allocation, missingness, censoring, contamination or selection makes the observed sample unrepresentative.
The evaluator’s mapping changes across time/version/context without an authorised construct change.
The decision boundary changes, especially after seeing results, without independent consequence/uncertainty justification.
Independent reference/bridge evidence shows the old measurement mapping is defective or stale; retrospective impact is assessed.
Optimisation improves the score while degrading, bypassing or relabelling the intended property.
Available evidence cannot identify which surface changed; the action must preserve the ambiguity rather than assign blame.

variation_and_control_model.requirement: Define unit, order, time base, opportunity/exposure, response owner and cost of false alarm, missed shift and delay.
Apply the measurement-system model before interpreting observed dispersion or chart signals.
Specify the local process/regime and whether prediction from a baseline is defensible; avoid mixed populations.
Model rational subgrouping, clustering, autocorrelation, seasonality and changing sample size/opportunity.
Keep control/detection limits separate from specifications/tolerances and from capability/performance claims.
Choose Shewhart, CUSUM/EWMA, residual, rare-event, multivariate or change-point logic for the shift and costs of interest.
Treat a signal as evidence that the assumed regime changed—not as proof of mechanism, guilt or moral attribution.
Investigate mechanism, avoid tampering with common-cause noise, and evaluate interventions against a preserved counterfactual/baseline.
Version and justify rebaselining, threshold changes and stale-control retirement; do not erase unfavourable history.

experiment_design_model.requirement: State the design alternative, causal contrast or prediction target, consequence threshold and consumer.
Identify the independently assignable unit and common-source structure; observations within a unit are not new replication.
Show the outcome/evaluator can resolve the smallest engineering-relevant effect and remains version-stable.
Randomise when feasible; otherwise state identification assumptions and use credible controls or mechanistic evidence.
Control known nuisance variation without post-hoc subgroup fishing; preserve randomisation within design constraints.
Use factorial/fractional/RSM structures when interactions or efficient multi-factor learning matter; document aliasing.
Count independent units/sources, not repeated reads, outputs, folds or same-seed reruns; model clusters/repeated measures.
Predefine or use valid adaptive/sequential boundaries; protect confirmation from exploratory flexibility.
Assess context, spillover, carryover, attrition, missingness and distribution shift before generalisation.
Report effect, uncertainty, engineering margin, assumptions and sensitivity; confirm optima or high-consequence claims independently.
Prefer the smallest design that separates live alternatives; omit formal DOE when an authoritative deterministic discriminator or exhaustive cheap search suffices.

sequential_evidence_and_stopping_model.rule: Freeze units, endpoint, analysis and sample size; do not repeatedly inspect and stop under a fixed-horizon calibration.
Choose SPRT, group-sequential/alpha-spending, confidence-sequence/always-valid or explicit Bayesian decision boundaries appropriate to the model and loss.
Another observation is worth buying only when it has a credible chance of changing the posterior/interval/boundary or the next engineering action after dependence and shared bias are considered.
Repeated measurements sharing unit, seed, batch, evaluator, dataset, reference or selection process contribute less—or no—independent information.
Stop when the decision alternatives are separated to the required consequence/uncertainty standard, including equivalence or futility where specified.
Stop when marginal information value is below cost or when a deterministic authority has already settled the claim.
Quota completion, favourable first crossing, repeated peeking under fixed-horizon rules, endpoint switching, or evaluator mutation after failure does not constitute evidential stopping.
New regime, material drift, changed construct, new failure mechanism or changed consequence can reopen evidence—but requires a new versioned decision contract.

robustness_reliability_and_tail_model.separation: Expected/central response under a defined population and use condition.
Dispersion across units, runs and nuisance factors; may change independently of the mean.
Quantiles, tolerance content, extremes and catastrophic-event uncertainty; not inferred from the mean alone.
Survival/failure/degradation across exposure with censoring and competing mechanisms.
Performance under specified nuisance, site, user, environment and distribution shifts.
Decision stability under plausible alternative distributions, dependence, transformations and extrapolation models.

proxy_and_evaluator_model.requirement: Define intended property, scoring rule, threshold, excluded cases and consequence before candidate exposure.
Use stable references/bridges to estimate candidate/process variation separately from evaluator/threshold variation.
A failing instrument may be changed only on independent evidence of measurement/construct defect, not because the candidate failed.
Record old/new evaluator, reasons, reference evidence, bridge performance and retrospective impact on all affected conclusions.
Search for score-preserving/property-breaking cases, selective exclusions, relabelled failures, post-hoc subgroups and test-set contamination.
Retain at least one outcome/reference not directly optimised by the governed actor when proxy capture is plausible.
Guard thresholds with consequence, uncertainty and comparability evidence; prohibit silent ratcheting or relaxation.
When candidate and evaluator change together, classify the result unresolved until a bridge or independent discriminator separates them.

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Define the decision-relevant measurand or construct before quantification
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Metrology’s measurand discipline, experimental operationalisation, and later construct-validity/invariance work.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: State what quantity or property is intended, under which conditions, before assigning a number.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A precise, reproducible number can answer the wrong question or represent an unstable proxy.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Construct substitution, category drift, metric availability being mistaken for decision relevance.
properties.MECHANISM: Bind each metric to a stated measurand/construct, unit of analysis, operating conditions, intended use, and disconfirming observations.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any measurement used to accept, reject, optimise, compare, or monitor an engineering state.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: When an authoritative deterministic fact directly answers the decision, record that fact rather than inventing a surrogate score.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Domain definition, decision owner, scope, and an explicit mapping from observations to the property of interest.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: The operational definition must preserve the distinctions the decision actually requires; an evaluator must not collapse relevant states.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: The construct is sufficiently coherent for the intended decision and its operationalisation does not change materially across samples.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents expensive optimisation of a convenient but irrelevant number and makes later uncertainty interpretable.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Design authority, test owner, regulator, operator, or other consumer of the decision.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Over-specifying the construct can delay cheap obvious decisions or disguise normative choices as technical definitions.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Under-definition permits proxy capture, post-hoc relabelling, and false agreement.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Ambiguous labels; changing definitions between baseline and candidate; composite scores whose weights hide trade-offs.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Metrology can define a measurand precisely while still leaving broader validity contested; formal latent constructs add model dependence.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from physical quantity definition toward explicit construct, context and decision-use validation.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: No metric governs until its intended property, scope, consumer, and admissible interpretation are fixed enough to be challenged.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A template or ontology is optional; the property is the explicit decision-linked definition.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Construct-validity evidence is domain-dependent; no universal statistical test establishes that a metric means what stakeholders intend.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should construct adequacy be stress-tested when the desired property is partly normative or changes with deployment context?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: What exact property is the target system claiming to measure?
Would two materially different states receive the same score?
Is an authoritative deterministic discriminator already available?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Establish measurement-system fitness before metric governance
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Eisenhart/NBS calibration-system evaluation, measurement assurance, gauge R&R, GUM and laboratory-quality systems.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Characterise the measurement process before treating its outputs as facts about the production process.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Observed variation may be dominated by instrument, operator, environment, fixture, algorithm, or evaluator variation.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Governing a candidate or process with a measurement system unable to discriminate decision-relevant states.
properties.MECHANISM: Estimate bias, repeatability, reproducibility, resolution, stability and uncertainty relative to the decision margin; block use when discrimination is inadequate.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Metrics near thresholds, comparisons whose expected effect is small, multi-operator/evaluator systems, or costly decisions.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a deterministic binary check with an authoritative oracle and negligible ambiguity, verify the oracle and use it directly rather than perform full MSA.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Defined measurand, representative items/conditions, reference or comparison basis, and a stated decision margin.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: The study must span the real operating range and relevant operators, instruments, environments and preprocessing paths.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Measurement error is reasonably estimable over the intended range and the study itself has not selected unusually easy samples.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Separates candidate/process variation from evaluator variation and reduces false corrective action.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Anyone relying on a metric, threshold, trend or experiment outcome.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Over-formal MSA can cost more than the decision and arbitrary percentage rules can reject a perfectly adequate binary discriminator.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Skipping MSA can make improvements, regressions and capability estimates indistinguishable from measurement noise.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Narrow part range; nonrepresentative operators; stable repeatability but unknown bias; passing a generic GR&R percentage unrelated to the decision.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Gauge R&R is only one design; destructive, automated, subjective and probabilistic evaluators require other designs.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from instrument calibration and variance decomposition to decision-specific evaluator capability and versioned validation.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Demonstrate enough discrimination for the intended decision, not abstract “good measurement,” and recheck after material evaluator change.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The form, software package, fixed 10×3×3 design or percentage cutoff is ceremony; decision-linked discrimination is the property.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: No single GR&R threshold is universally optimal; measurement investment depends on decision loss and achievable resolution.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should measurement fitness be quantified for adaptive, generative or partly subjective evaluators?

VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.DECISION_PROBLEM: Decide whether observed process/candidate differences exceed measurement variation.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.ASSUMED_DATA_GENERATING_PROCESS: True state plus instrument/operator/environment/evaluator error, possibly heteroscedastic or drifting.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Representative range, repeated measures, reference comparisons and version control.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.SIGNAL_OR_DISCRIMINATOR: Variance/bias/uncertainty small enough relative to the decision margin.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_POSITIVE_COST: Unnecessary redesign or rejection caused by measurement noise.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_NEGATIVE_COST: A real defect hidden by poor resolution or attenuation.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.NONSTATIONARITY_RISK: Calibration/evaluator drift can invalidate earlier decomposition.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.INTERVENTION_RISK: Changing the candidate to chase evaluator noise; changing the evaluator to erase a candidate failure.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Direct authoritative check or coarse decision with a very wide margin.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Decision-specific measurement-capability gate with ongoing checks.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Can the target measurement system discriminate the states that change the decision?
How much observed variation is evaluator rather than candidate variation?
Would the conclusion survive another competent operator, fixture or evaluator version?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Calibration and metrological traceability where decision-relevant
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Physical metrology, calibration hierarchies, VIM/GUM and ISO/IEC 17025.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Relate measurement results to references through a documented calibration chain with stated uncertainty.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A stable instrument can be consistently offset, incomparable across sites, or anchored to an obsolete reference.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: False comparability, hidden bias, ungrounded units and calibration labels treated as universal validity.
properties.MECHANISM: Use suitable standards/reference methods, record calibration state and uncertainty contributions, and maintain traceability at the result level.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Physical/chemical measurements, regulated tolerances, interlaboratory exchange, or any decision requiring comparability to a standard.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For purely ordinal/local decisions with a verified internal reference and no cross-context claim, full national/international traceability may add no value.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Valid calibration method, competent execution, suitable reference, environmental controls, and an uncertainty chain.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Calibration points and standards must cover the range, matrix and conditions of use.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: The reference hierarchy and calibration model remain applicable; no unmodelled transport or nonlinear effects dominate.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Makes results comparable, exposes bias/uncertainty and supports defensible conformance decisions.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Laboratory, manufacturer, customer, regulator and downstream analysts.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Calibration theatre can consume resources while routine use, sampling or construct definition remains defective.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Absent or stale calibration can produce confident but systematically wrong decisions.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: “NIST-traceable” asserted for an organisation; calibration certificate without uncertainty; traceability outside the working range.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: NIST explicitly rejects treating traceability as a guarantee of fitness for purpose or absence of mistakes.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from periodic instrument adjustment to result-specific traceability plus ongoing measurement assurance.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Require the level of traceability needed for comparability and decision risk, alongside—not instead of—fitness validation.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A certificate, logo or fixed interval is not the property; the evidence chain and decision fitness are.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Some digital/subjective measurements lack a meaningful SI chain; analogous provenance does not equal metrological traceability.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What is the minimum defensible reference chain for nonphysical evaluators and rapidly changing benchmarks?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Does the result—not merely the instrument—have a documented reference chain and uncertainty?
Is cross-site or cross-version comparability actually required for this decision?
Could a local deterministic reference provide a cheaper adequate path?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Keep bias/accuracy distinct from precision
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Classical measurement error, NBS measurement evaluation, ISO 5725 and VIM.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Separate systematic displacement from random dispersion and estimate each against a reference/use case.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Highly repeatable measurements can be systematically wrong; averaging reduces random error but not shared bias.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: False confidence from tight distributions, many decimals, or repeated agreement around the wrong value.
properties.MECHANISM: Compare to suitable references/alternatives for bias while estimating dispersion under repeatability and reproducibility conditions.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Whenever magnitude or direction relative to truth/standard matters, especially near limits.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: If the decision is invariant to a known constant offset and only ranks within one stable system, bias correction may be unnecessary—but must be explicit.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Reference value or defensible triangulation, representative operating range and stable calibration/evaluator state.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Enough resolution and coverage to detect both offset and dispersion; uncertainty in the reference included.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Bias is reasonably stable or modelled over range/context; reference is more informative than the system under test.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents repeated measurement from converting shared bias into narrow but false confidence.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Measurement owner and decision consumer.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Over-correcting an uncertain estimated bias can add variance or create discontinuities.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Ignoring bias can leave every repeated test green while the underlying property remains wrong.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Using correlation as accuracy; reporting only standard deviation; reference standard shares the same bias.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Using correlation as accuracy; reporting only standard deviation; reference standard shares the same bias. Contrary evidence/limit: For complex construct measures, “true value” may be unavailable; bias must then be bounded through convergent/criterion evidence rather than asserted.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Modern practice reports trueness/bias, precision and uncertainty rather than one undifferentiated “accuracy” score.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Decision-specific decomposition of systematic and random error, with correction only when validated.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Extra decimal places and repeated readings are ceremony when the dominant error is systematic.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: For complex construct measures, “true value” may be unavailable; bias must then be bounded through convergent/criterion evidence rather than asserted.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can shared-method bias be detected when all available reference systems inherit common training data or assumptions?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Could the target evaluator be consistently wrong despite excellent repeatability?
What independent reference or triangulation checks bias?
Would more repetitions reduce the dominant uncertainty component?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Distinguish repeatability, reproducibility and validity
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Interlaboratory measurement science, ISO 5725, gauge R&R, rater reliability and reproducibility debates.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Estimate same-condition variation separately from operator/site/instrument/context variation.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A result may repeat under one setup but fail across competent operators or contexts; both may repeat an invalid construct.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Treating identical reruns as independent corroboration or interpreting consistency as truth.
properties.MECHANISM: Design crossed/nested comparisons over relevant operators, instruments, sites, times and methods; assess validity separately.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Multi-operator, multi-site, automated evaluator, stochastic test or claimed general result.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For one-use, one-instrument local control with no transfer claim and a wide margin, a limited stability check may suffice.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Representative factors and levels, randomisation/order control, clear agreement target and adequate item range.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Measurement outputs are comparable and evaluator versions are fixed/documented during the study.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Factor effects and interactions can be estimated; repeated conditions approximate intended routine use.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents pseudo-replication and hidden operator/evaluator sensitivity.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Measurement owner, experimenter and anyone claiming portability.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Demanding universal reproducibility can reject legitimately context-specific measurements.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Testing only repeatability misses site/operator/context failures and shared invalidity.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Confusing reproducibility with exact equality; narrow sample range; no validity criterion; treating reruns as new evidence.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Confusing reproducibility with exact equality; narrow sample range; no validity criterion; treating reruns as new evidence. Contrary evidence/limit: Definitions of “reproducibility” vary across metrology and science; the factors changed must always be stated.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from instrument precision to interlaboratory, computational and evaluator-version reproducibility, while retaining validity as a separate burden.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Claim only the level of stability actually tested, and never infer validity from repeatability alone.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A standard GR&R worksheet is optional; the factor-appropriate variance/agreement design is the property.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Definitions of “reproducibility” vary across metrology and science; the factors changed must always be stated.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should reproducibility be defined for non-deterministic systems whose output distribution, not individual output, is the object?

EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.HYPOTHESIS_OR_DECISION: Determine whether measurement conclusions survive relevant changes of operator/instrument/site/context.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPERIMENTAL_UNIT: Measured item under a specified factor combination.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INDEPENDENCE_ASSUMPTION: Repeated items or clusters must be modelled; repeated readings on one item are not independent items.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.RANDOMISATION_OR_CONTROL: Randomise order where drift/learning/carryover is possible.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.BLOCKING_OR_STRATIFICATION: Block by item/batch/context when nuisance variation is large.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.REPLICATION_MEANING: Replication means new independent items or justified repeated-measures modelling, not duplicated records.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INTERACTION_RISK: Operator×item and context×method interactions can dominate.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.STOPPING_RULE: Pre-specify precision/agreement targets and analysis before inspecting favourable subsets.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Quantifies which variation source threatens the decision.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.COST: Additional operators/sites/items and possibly destructive samples.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED: A maximal study may be wasteful for a narrow local use.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Factor-matched reproducibility study plus separate validity evidence.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Are repeated results same-condition repeatability or genuinely cross-condition reproducibility?
Which operator, site, seed, environment or evaluator factors were varied?
What evidence addresses validity rather than consistency?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Match resolution, sensitivity, specificity and threshold discrimination to the decision
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Instrument resolution/metrology, diagnostic classification, ROC analysis and conformity-assessment decision rules.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Ensure the measurement/classifier can separate states on opposite sides of the action boundary.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A coarse or poorly discriminating evaluator makes candidate and measurement variation observationally inseparable.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: False passes/fails hidden by a precise-looking continuous score or an arbitrary threshold.
properties.MECHANISM: Characterise resolution and class-conditional error across the operating range; choose thresholds using consequence-weighted false-positive/false-negative risks.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Threshold decisions, defect detection, rare-event screens, small expected improvements, or changing class prevalence.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: When a deterministic authoritative predicate directly distinguishes states, use it instead of estimating sensitivity/specificity.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable labels/reference adjudication, representative prevalence/spectrum, stated loss asymmetry and threshold version.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Reference labels are sufficiently accurate and the validation set represents intended use; resolution is not inflated by preprocessing leakage.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Future cases are drawn from a relevant population or shift is monitored; class definitions remain stable.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces threshold gaming and makes error trade-offs visible.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Decision owner, safety/quality gate, monitoring operator.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Optimising sensitivity can create alert floods; optimising specificity can hide rare costly defects.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: A low-power detector can report no change while meaningful failures accumulate.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Selecting threshold on the same test set; ignoring prevalence; changing expected answers after failures; resolution below tolerance width.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Selecting threshold on the same test set; ignoring prevalence; changing expected answers after failures; resolution below tolerance width. Contrary evidence/limit: ROC-like summaries may obscure calibration, prevalence shift and heterogeneous costs; no single threshold is universally optimal.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from instrument least count and fixed cutoffs to calibrated decision rules, guard bands, ROC/utility analysis and drift checks.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use the cheapest discriminator whose error profile is adequate for the decision and freeze/version its threshold unless independent recalibration evidence exists.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A universal “90% accuracy” or fixed sigma cutoff is ceremony; the decision-specific error surface is the property.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: ROC-like summaries may obscure calibration, prevalence shift and heterogeneous costs; no single threshold is universally optimal.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should threshold uncertainty be propagated when both labels and prevalence drift?

VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.DECISION_PROBLEM: Choose and maintain an action threshold under measurement error and changing prevalence.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.ASSUMED_DATA_GENERATING_PROCESS: Latent state observed through a noisy score/classifier with class-conditional errors.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Representative reference labels, uncertainty and threshold versioning.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.SIGNAL_OR_DISCRIMINATOR: Stable separation/calibration sufficient for consequence-weighted decision.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_POSITIVE_COST: Alert burden, needless rejection or process tampering.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_NEGATIVE_COST: Missed defect or false assurance.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.NONSTATIONARITY_RISK: Prevalence/concept drift changes predictive values and optimal threshold.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.INTERVENTION_RISK: Post-failure threshold movement can reward-hack the metric.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Authoritative deterministic predicate with negligible ambiguity.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Guard-banded/versioned threshold with periodic independent validation.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: What false-pass and false-fail rates matter at the actual threshold?
Is the evaluator’s resolution small enough relative to the decision margin?
Can a threshold change be justified on evidence independent of the failed candidate?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Carry measurement uncertainty into engineering decisions
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: GUM uncertainty budgets, calibration science and conformity-assessment decision rules.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Identify material uncertainty components, combine them appropriately and report their relation to the decision boundary.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Point estimates and binary labels can conceal that the decision is not actually discriminated.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: False precision, unsupported conformance, and treating reference or model uncertainty as zero.
properties.MECHANISM: Build an uncertainty model/budget, propagate components and use intervals, guard bands or explicit loss-based rules.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Measurements close to specifications, comparisons with small effects, extrapolations, and regulated claims.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: When the result is far from every relevant boundary and a conservative worst-case bound suffices, a detailed budget may be unnecessary.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Defined measurand/model, traceable components where applicable, covariance handling, and a stated coverage/decision rule.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Inputs and correlations are characterised over the intended regime; software/preprocessing uncertainty included when material.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: The propagation model is adequate; uncertainty is not silently conditional on fixed but uncertain calibration/model choices.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents binary overclaim and directs effort toward dominant uncertainty components.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Conformance authority, designer, customer or risk owner.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Excessively conservative stacking can reject useful systems and encourage uninformative complexity.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Ignoring uncertainty makes near-boundary decisions appear decisive and weakens reproducibility.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Double-counted components; omitted covariance; confidence interval mislabeled as tolerance interval; uncertainty reported without decision use.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Double-counted components; omitted covariance; confidence interval mislabeled as tolerance interval; uncertainty reported without decision use. Contrary evidence/limit: GUM-style propagation can be strained by nonlinearity, asymmetric tails, model uncertainty and adaptive algorithms; simulation/Bayesian or interval methods may be needed.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from error margins to structured budgets and decision rules linking uncertainty to false accept/reject risks.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use proportionate uncertainty analysis sufficient to show whether the next action is discriminated.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A long budget is ceremony if a dominant bound already resolves the decision; conversely, “±” without a model is decorative.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: GUM-style propagation can be strained by nonlinearity, asymmetric tails, model uncertainty and adaptive algorithms; simulation/Bayesian or interval methods may be needed.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should epistemic model uncertainty and evaluator retraining uncertainty be integrated without false numerical precision?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Would plausible measurement uncertainty cross the action boundary?
Which uncertainty component dominates, and can it be reduced economically?
Is the interval about a parameter, future observation, or population content?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Evaluate inter-rater/evaluator agreement with a design matched to use
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Interlaboratory precision, ICC families, method-comparison and modern evaluator studies.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Quantify agreement, not merely correlation, under the exact rater/evaluator sampling and decision target.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Evaluators can rank cases similarly while disagreeing materially in level or pass/fail outcome.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Stable-looking scores that vary by evaluator, rubric interpretation, operator or model version.
properties.MECHANISM: Use paired/crossed items, blinded/randomised order, agreement-appropriate ICC/kappa/difference analyses, disagreement adjudication and subgroup checks.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Subjective ratings, manual inspection, model judging, multi-laboratory tests, or operator-dependent measurements.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A deterministic reference rule with auditable outputs may need spot verification rather than a full agreement study.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Representative difficult/easy items, sufficient rater diversity, stable rubric, and a declared agreement target.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Raters/evaluators are independent enough to expose variation rather than copied or trained on identical answers.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: The selected agreement statistic matches fixed/random raters, absolute agreement/consistency and scale properties.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reveals evaluator variance and cases where no stable decision exists.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Test owner, adjudicator, quality gate and downstream experimenter.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Forcing consensus can erase legitimate ambiguity or minority expertise.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Ignoring disagreement converts evaluator identity into hidden treatment.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Using Pearson correlation; prevalence-sensitive kappa without context; shared rubric bias; adjudicating after seeing candidate identity.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Using Pearson correlation; prevalence-sensitive kappa without context; shared rubric bias; adjudicating after seeing candidate identity. Contrary evidence/limit: Agreement can be high because cases are homogeneous or decisions trivial; validity and representativeness remain separate.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from precision/reproducibility studies to versioned evaluator ensembles and explicit adjudication.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Report disagreement structure, not only one coefficient; block governance where disagreement crosses decision boundaries.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A fashionable reliability coefficient or arbitrary cutoff is not the property.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Agreement can be high because cases are homogeneous or decisions trivial; validity and representativeness remain separate.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How much independent evaluator diversity is needed before agreement adds evidence rather than multiplicity theatre?

EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.HYPOTHESIS_OR_DECISION: Determine whether evaluator identity changes the engineering conclusion.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPERIMENTAL_UNIT: Item×evaluator judgement, with item as the generalisation unit.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INDEPENDENCE_ASSUMPTION: Multiple ratings of one item are clustered; evaluators may share training/rubric dependence.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.RANDOMISATION_OR_CONTROL: Randomise/blind order and candidate identity where possible.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.BLOCKING_OR_STRATIFICATION: Stratify by item difficulty/context and evaluator type.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.REPLICATION_MEANING: Independent items and independently formed judgements, not duplicated outputs.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INTERACTION_RISK: Evaluator×item interactions identify ambiguous regions.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.STOPPING_RULE: Predefine agreement target and adjudication protocol.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Separates stable decisions from evaluator-sensitive ones.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.COST: Rater time, adjudication and representative case construction.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED: Excessive panels can create consensus bureaucracy and common-mode bias.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Decision-linked agreement study plus construct-validity checks.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Do evaluators agree on the actual action, not just rank ordering?
Were difficult and boundary cases represented?
Could shared training data or rubric bias make agreement non-independent?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Test measurement invariance and transport across contexts
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Interlaboratory comparison, psychometric invariance, dataset-shift analysis and robust measurement practice.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Check whether the same score has the same interpretation across sites, populations, environments, versions or time.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A metric may be stable locally yet change meaning under population mix, language, hardware, operator or deployment context.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Invalid cross-context comparisons, hidden subgroup bias and false trend attribution.
properties.MECHANISM: Specify transport claim, compare calibration/error/construct structure across contexts, and restrict claims or recalibrate when invariance fails.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Cross-site benchmarking, longitudinal monitoring, heterogeneous users, distribution shift or environment changes.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: No invariance study is needed for an explicitly local, one-time decision that makes no comparison beyond its validated context.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Comparable reference outcomes, sufficient overlap/coverage, versioned context metadata and a plausible transport model.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: The measurement process and sampling frame are observable enough to distinguish construct shift from composition shift.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Observed contexts span the intended deployment; unobserved effect modifiers are bounded or acknowledged.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents scores from being treated as universal when they are context-indexed.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Benchmark owner, product/system decision maker, regulator or cross-site analyst.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Over-demanding invariance may suppress legitimate context-specific adaptation.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: No check permits silent construct drift and unfair/unsafe threshold transfer.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Aggregate invariance hiding subgroup failure; recalibration on contaminated outcomes; using identical preprocessing as proof of meaning.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Aggregate invariance hiding subgroup failure; recalibration on contaminated outcomes; using identical preprocessing as proof of meaning. Contrary evidence/limit: No finite study guarantees future invariance under open-ended distribution shift; monitoring and bounded claims are required.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from interlaboratory reproducibility to formal invariance, calibration transport and shift monitoring.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Claim equivalence only over tested contexts; otherwise maintain context-specific calibration or explicit uncertainty.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: One global score or normalisation recipe is ceremony when meanings differ.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: No finite study guarantees future invariance under open-ended distribution shift; monitoring and bounded claims are required.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which context dimensions must be covered before a metric can support a general engineering claim?

VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.DECISION_PROBLEM: Decide whether a change in score reflects a changed target state or changed measurement context.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.ASSUMED_DATA_GENERATING_PROCESS: Context-indexed latent property observed through context-sensitive measurement and sampling.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Comparable anchors/reference outcomes and context metadata.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.SIGNAL_OR_DISCRIMINATOR: Stable calibration/construct relation or an identified context effect.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_POSITIVE_COST: False process intervention due to composition/evaluator shift.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_NEGATIVE_COST: Failure to detect real subgroup/context degradation.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.NONSTATIONARITY_RISK: High: deployment populations and instruments evolve.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.INTERVENTION_RISK: Global recalibration can erase local failures; local tuning can destroy comparability.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Restrict the claim to the validated context.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Versioned context-specific calibration with transport tests and drift alarms.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Has the score retained calibration and meaning across the contexts being compared?
Could a changed population mix explain the apparent process change?
Is a context-specific metric safer than forced global invariance?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Monitor evaluator/instrument drift and require independent recalibration evidence
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Check standards and measurement assurance, control of calibration systems, longitudinal rater/benchmark stability.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Treat the measurement system as a process that can drift, not a one-time certified constant.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Apparent candidate/process change may be caused by aging sensors, changed operators, rubric edits, data refreshes or threshold movement.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Attributing measurement change to the object; changing the evaluator after failure until a pass appears.
properties.MECHANISM: Use stable check/reference samples, bridge studies, version control, drift limits and independent change justification before recalibration.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Long-lived controls, automated scoring, model-based evaluators, changing laboratories or any metric with material maintenance.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a one-shot destructive test with contemporaneous references, ongoing drift monitoring may be impossible; preserve calibration evidence and uncertainty instead.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Reference/check material stable enough to detect drift, bridge overlap between versions, and governance independent of candidate outcome.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Check samples represent important ranges and are protected from optimisation/contamination.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Reference drift is slower or independently detectable; repeated checks are not all affected by the same environmental cause.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Preserves comparability and prevents evaluator mutation from masquerading as improvement.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Measurement owner, release/acceptance authority and audit consumer.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Over-sensitive drift rules create churn; frozen obsolete evaluators can also become invalid.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: No drift detection can systematically misclassify every subsequent candidate or hide concept change.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Rebaselining after alarms; editing expected answers after seeing failures; check-set overfitting; no version bridge.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Rebaselining after alarms; editing expected answers after seeing failures; check-set overfitting; no version bridge. Contrary evidence/limit: Reference materials and holdouts can themselves age, leak or become unrepresentative; drift detection has no absolute anchor without external refresh.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from physical check standards to benchmark holdouts, blind audits, bridge datasets and change-control evidence.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Recalibrate when independent evidence shows measurement defect or context change; preserve old/new bridge and re-evaluate prior conclusions where material.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A calendar recalibration interval or automatic threshold refresh is not the property.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Reference materials and holdouts can themselves age, leak or become unrepresentative; drift detection has no absolute anchor without external refresh.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should old conclusions be revisited after a material evaluator recalibration?

VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.DECISION_PROBLEM: Detect whether the measurement process, rather than the object, has changed.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.ASSUMED_DATA_GENERATING_PROCESS: Stable/slowly varying references observed through a potentially drifting evaluator.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Protected check samples, version metadata and bridge overlap.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.SIGNAL_OR_DISCRIMINATOR: Reference/control deviation beyond a consequence-weighted drift boundary.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_POSITIVE_COST: Unnecessary recalibration and broken comparability.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_NEGATIVE_COST: Persistent biased governance or hidden evaluator degradation.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.NONSTATIONARITY_RISK: Reference populations and constructs may drift too.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.INTERVENTION_RISK: Rebaselining to current outputs can erase evidence.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Manual reference comparison before a high-stakes decision.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Independent bridge study, versioned change control and bounded revalidation.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: What evidence distinguishes evaluator drift from candidate/process change?
Was recalibration justified using evidence independent of the failed candidate?
Is there a bridge allowing old and new evaluator versions to be compared?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Use representative reference standards and challenge shared-reference bias
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Calibration artefacts, measurement assurance samples, proficiency testing and method-comparison practice.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Validate against references/check samples spanning the real operating range and difficult conditions.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A measurement system can perform well on ideal standards while failing on routine matrices, edge cases or degraded specimens.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: False validation from easy, narrow, contaminated or common-mode reference samples.
properties.MECHANISM: Select reference items by intended-use strata and failure mechanisms; use independent methods/sources where shared bias is plausible.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Calibration transfer, evaluator validation, threshold setting and cross-site comparison.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a single known artefact or exact digital identity check, one authoritative reference may be enough.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable assigned values with uncertainty, representative coverage and documented provenance.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Reference uncertainty and commutability/representativeness are known; reference items are not leaked into optimisation.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Sampled references cover decision-relevant variability and do not share all defects with the candidate measurement.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Finds context-specific bias and reduces benchmark overfitting.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Calibration laboratory, evaluator owner and downstream decision maker.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Broad reference programmes can be costly and still miss unknown unknowns.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Narrow references can certify a system that fails precisely where decisions are hardest.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Using only pristine standards; treating consensus as truth; reusing public benchmarks until memorised; excluding failures from the reference pool.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Using only pristine standards; treating consensus as truth; reusing public benchmarks until memorised; excluding failures from the reference pool. Contrary evidence/limit: Representativeness cannot be proven exhaustively; rare or emerging failure modes may be absent.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from physical reference artefacts to commutable samples, proficiency tests, blind holdouts and multi-method triangulation.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Reference evidence is valid only for the covered range/context and must be protected from optimisation.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A named standard material or benchmark is not sufficient if it is nonrepresentative.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Representativeness cannot be proven exhaustively; rare or emerging failure modes may be absent.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can reference sets be refreshed without destroying longitudinal comparability or leaking the target?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Do reference samples span actual boundary and failure cases?
Could candidate and reference share the same systematic defect?
Has optimisation exposure contaminated the reference set?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Preserve data provenance, preprocessing, version and lineage
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Laboratory records/traceability, reproducible analysis, adaptive-data concerns and modern data governance.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Record where observations came from, how they were selected/transformed, and which evaluator/code/threshold version produced each result.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Untracked filtering, deduplication, relabelling or evaluator changes can manufacture an apparent effect.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Irreproducible evidence, hidden leakage, duplicate evidence and inability to separate data change from process change.
properties.MECHANISM: Use immutable identifiers, transformation logs, selection/exclusion reasons, versioned code/configuration and lineage-aware aggregation.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any multi-stage analysis, reused benchmark, merged source, adaptive evaluation or longitudinal comparison.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A small manually inspectable deterministic dataset may need only a concise signed record, not a full data platform.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable identifiers, access controls, timestamp/version semantics and retention of raw or authoritative source where lawful.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Preprocessing is deterministic or its randomness/configuration is recorded; lineage captures duplication and dependence.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Recorded provenance is complete enough to reconstruct decision-relevant transformations.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Enables replication, dependence detection, rollback and attribution of evaluator/data changes.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Analyst, reviewer, regulator, future maintainer and experiment consumer.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Heavy lineage systems can become compliance theatre and create privacy/security cost.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Missing lineage allows cherry-picking, test contamination and false multiplicity.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Overwriting raw data; undocumented manual fixes; copied observations counted as independent; changing labels without bridge.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Overwriting raw data; undocumented manual fixes; copied observations counted as independent; changing labels without bridge. Contrary evidence/limit: Provenance proves what happened, not that the recorded process was unbiased or valid.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from laboratory notebooks/calibration certificates to executable pipelines, dataset/evaluator cards and contamination controls.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Preserve the minimum complete lineage needed to reconstruct the evidence and its dependence structure.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A particular tool, schema or immutable ledger is optional; reconstructability and identity are the property.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Provenance proves what happened, not that the recorded process was unbiased or valid.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What lineage granularity is sufficient to detect common-source dependence without imposing prohibitive cost?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Can every reported result be tied to exact data, preprocessing, evaluator and threshold versions?
Are duplicated or derived observations being counted as independent evidence?
Can excluded measurements be audited with reasons?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Model missingness, censoring, exclusions and selection mechanisms
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Sampling theory, Rubin missing-data framework, reliability censoring and selective-reporting criticism.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Treat absence/exclusion as part of the data-generating and observation process rather than silently deleting it.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Failures may be missing, censored or excluded non-randomly, biasing rates, lifetimes and comparisons.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Survivorship bias, complete-case bias, favourable subgroup selection and underreported failure tails.
properties.MECHANISM: Record reasons/timing, define censoring, analyse sensitivity under plausible mechanisms, and use design/model methods only when assumptions are defensible.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Dropout, time-limited tests, incomplete logs, destructive failures, filtered benchmark items or unobserved outcomes.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: If missingness is demonstrably negligible and unrelated to outcome/exposure, transparent complete-case treatment may be adequate.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Provenance of attempted units, exposure time/opportunity, selection rule and reason codes.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: The system distinguishes “not observed,” “not applicable,” “failed before measurement,” and deliberate exclusion.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Chosen MAR/MCAR/censoring/selection assumptions approximate reality; sensitivity bounds cover uncertainty.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents falsely optimistic rates and clarifies which population the result describes.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Reliability analyst, experimenter, quality gate and consumer of aggregate metrics.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Over-modelled imputation can inject unjustified information and narrow uncertainty.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Ignoring informative missingness can reverse conclusions or erase catastrophic cases.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Calling failures “invalid”; censoring at different risk states; post-hoc subgroup restriction; imputation model trained on outcome leakage.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Calling failures “invalid”; censoring at different risk states; post-hoc subgroup restriction; imputation model trained on outcome leakage. Contrary evidence/limit: Missing-not-at-random mechanisms are generally not identified from observed data alone; sensitivity/partial identification may be the honest endpoint.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from simple complete-case analysis to explicit missingness mechanisms, survival methods, inverse weighting/bounds and sensitivity analysis.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Make the observation/selection process auditable and report conclusions conditional on or robust to plausible missingness mechanisms.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Automatic imputation or a missing-data checklist is not the property.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Missing-not-at-random mechanisms are generally not identified from observed data alone; sensitivity/partial identification may be the honest endpoint.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which missingness mechanisms are distinguishable with available auxiliary/process data?

EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.HYPOTHESIS_OR_DECISION: Estimate effect/performance despite incomplete outcomes without hiding selection.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPERIMENTAL_UNIT: Originally eligible experimental or observational unit, including censored units.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INDEPENDENCE_ASSUMPTION: Missingness can induce dependence/selection; clusters remain clusters.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.RANDOMISATION_OR_CONTROL: Randomisation protects assignment but not post-assignment missingness.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.BLOCKING_OR_STRATIFICATION: Stratify/design follow-up around predictors of missingness.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.REPLICATION_MEANING: Replication counts eligible independent units, not only completed observations.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INTERACTION_RISK: Treatment/context can interact with dropout/censoring.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.STOPPING_RULE: Pre-specify exclusion and censoring rules; document deviations.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Recovers or bounds decision-relevant estimates and exposes uncertainty.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.COST: Follow-up, instrumentation and larger sample requirements.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED: Complex imputation can become decorative if assumptions are unknowable.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Transparent mechanism model plus sensitivity/bounds and all-unit accounting.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Which attempted units or outcomes are absent, censored or excluded?
Could exclusion probability depend on failure severity or candidate identity?
Would plausible missing-not-at-random scenarios change the decision?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Account for measurement intervention, destruction and contamination
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Destructive inspection/acceptance sampling, test-effect/carryover design, measurement assurance and sensor intrusiveness.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Recognise that observing can consume, stress, train, prime, cache or otherwise alter the unit/system and later evidence.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Repeated measurements may not be exchangeable because the first test changes the candidate, operator or environment.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Pseudo-replication, induced failures, test-set learning and claiming non-destructive evidence from altered units.
properties.MECHANISM: Classify measurement as destructive/intrusive, randomise order, use fresh units or washout/holdouts, and model carryover when unavoidable.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Destructive material tests, accelerated stress, human/agent learning, repeated benchmark exposure, cache/warm-up effects.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: When a verified measurement is genuinely non-invasive and order-invariant, ordinary repeated-measures methods may suffice.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Defined experimental unit, exposure history, test order, fresh-unit availability and a mechanism for intervention effects.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Provenance records prior exposures and distinguishes unit reuse from independent replication.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Carryover/washout model is plausible or fresh independent units are available.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents repeated testing from manufacturing the very behaviour it purports to measure.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Experiment designer, reliability/test engineer and benchmark owner.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Fresh-unit requirements can be expensive, unethical or impossible; overly strict rules can block learning.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Ignoring intervention can produce optimistic adaptation or pessimistic stress damage.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Calling warmed/cached retries independent; destructive test sample not representative; training on failed benchmark items; inadequate washout.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Calling warmed/cached retries independent; destructive test sample not representative; training on failed benchmark items; inadequate washout. Contrary evidence/limit: In adaptive systems, measurement and improvement may be inseparable by design; the goal becomes explicit online-learning evaluation rather than pretending independence.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from destructive sampling and crossover design to explicit benchmark exposure and adaptive-system contamination controls.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use fresh or counterbalanced units where material; otherwise model and report intervention history and limit claims.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A blanket ban on retesting is not the property; exposure-aware evidence is.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: In adaptive systems, measurement and improvement may be inseparable by design; the goal becomes explicit online-learning evaluation rather than pretending independence.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: When is reuse acceptable because the deployment itself includes learning from feedback?

EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.HYPOTHESIS_OR_DECISION: Determine performance/effect without confounding it with prior measurement exposure.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPERIMENTAL_UNIT: Fresh unit or explicitly exposure-indexed repeated unit.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INDEPENDENCE_ASSUMPTION: Repeated observations on altered units are dependent.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.RANDOMISATION_OR_CONTROL: Randomise test order/exposure; use controls or fresh units.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.BLOCKING_OR_STRATIFICATION: Block by batch, order, prior exposure or stress level.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.REPLICATION_MEANING: Independent replication requires unexposed units or a correct carryover model.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INTERACTION_RISK: Exposure×candidate/context interactions may be the main effect.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.STOPPING_RULE: Predefine retest/washout and stopping rules.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Separates intrinsic behaviour from measurement-induced adaptation/damage.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.COST: Fresh samples, destructive loss, washout time.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED: Full fresh-unit designs may be prohibitive.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Exposure-aware design with fresh-unit cheap path only where decision consequences justify it.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Does running the measurement change the unit, evaluator, cache, operator or future candidate?
Are retries fresh independent units or exposed repetitions?
Is test exposure part of the intended deployment, and if so is it evaluated as such?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Discriminate routine/common variation from evidence of a changed process
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Shewhart’s Bell Labs statistical control and later common/special-cause translation.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Use time-ordered evidence to distinguish an approximately stable pattern from departures worth investigation.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Treating every fluctuation as actionable or averaging away a real process change.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Tampering, alert fatigue, blame, missed assignable mechanisms and invalid prediction from unstable data.
properties.MECHANISM: Establish a relevant baseline, plot/model observations in time order, use calibrated signals, and investigate mechanisms rather than equate alarms with causes.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Repeated process output where a stable-enough reference regime and actionable changes are plausible.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a deterministic failure with an authoritative cause, repair it directly; for one-off heterogeneous work with no repeatable unit, causal case analysis may dominate charting.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Defined process/stream, chronological data, adequate measurement, comparable opportunities and a consequence-linked response plan.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Measurement error is small enough and evaluator drift is separated from process drift.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: The baseline is sufficiently homogeneous/stable for the chosen chart/model; dependence and mixtures are handled.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces noise-chasing while creating earlier evidence of meaningful change.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Process owner and investigator—not a mechanism-free automated punishment system.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: A signal may be a false alarm or harmless change; investigation/adjustment can destabilise the process.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Weak signals or poor measurement can miss slow, small or rare harmful changes.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Control limits treated as specs; alarms treated as causes; retrospective cherry-picking; rebaselining away failures; worker blame.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The two-cause vocabulary can oversimplify continuous, interacting and drifting sources; “special” is statistical, not moral or personal.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from Shewhart charts to CUSUM/EWMA, time-series/residual, change-point and context-specific monitoring with explicit costs.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use the lightest calibrated discriminator that separates expected variation from actionable change, then require causal investigation before intervention.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The property is discrimination and response discipline, not putting every metric on a three-sigma chart.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: In highly adaptive or nonstationary systems there may be no enduring common-cause baseline; change detection must be reframed around local regimes or forecasts.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What level of local stability is sufficient for useful monitoring in continuously changing systems?

VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.DECISION_PROBLEM: Decide when a process departure warrants investigation or intervention.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.ASSUMED_DATA_GENERATING_PROCESS: Approximately stable baseline plus occasional changes, or an explicitly modelled dynamic process.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Time-ordered comparable measurements with controlled evaluator variation.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.SIGNAL_OR_DISCRIMINATOR: A signal with known/estimated operating characteristics relative to a target change.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_POSITIVE_COST: Wasted investigation, alert fatigue and tampering.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_NEGATIVE_COST: Undetected degradation or delayed containment.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.NONSTATIONARITY_RISK: High if the baseline, population or operating policy changes.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.INTERVENTION_RISK: Immediate adjustment to noise can increase variation and obscure causes.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Direct mechanism evidence or a simple visual/time-order check for large changes.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Calibrated monitoring plus investigation, error costs and rebaseline governance.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Does the target system distinguish expected variation from evidence of a changed process?
Is a chart signal being mistaken for a proven causal mechanism?
Could the apparent change instead be evaluator or population drift?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Choose rational subgroups and model dependence rather than count correlated observations as sample size
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Shewhart subgroup logic, time-series SPC and pseudoreplication criticism.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Arrange within/between-group comparisons so the statistic reflects the variation source relevant to the decision.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Subgroups can mix different regimes or repeated readings can masquerade as independent evidence.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Wrong control limits, attenuated/expanded uncertainty, false replication and concealed between-batch/time effects.
properties.MECHANISM: Define the process unit and correlation structure; subgroup items exposed to common short-term conditions when that answers the decision, or use cluster/time-series models.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Batch, lot, repeated-run, time-series, nested, clustered or same-seed/same-environment observations.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: When observations are demonstrably independent and identically produced at the decision scale, ordinary independent analysis is adequate.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Process map, timestamps/batch/seed/operator identifiers, enough clusters/subgroups and a defensible within/between variation interpretation.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Measurement repeats are labelled separately from production units; common-source dependence is observable.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Within-subgroup homogeneity and between-subgroup opportunity for relevant change, or a valid dependence model.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Corrects effective sample size and makes signals interpretable at the intervention scale.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Monitoring designer, experimenter and evidence consumer.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Overly narrow subgroups can hide important within-window heterogeneity; complex models can reduce transparency.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Ignoring dependence yields false precision and repeated green checks that are informationally redundant.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Convenience subgroups; averaging across shifts; treating multiple outputs from one run as independent; one cluster per condition.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: “Rational subgroup” is not a magic recipe; it encodes a causal/process judgement and may fail in low-volume/high-mix work.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from subgroup construction rules to hierarchical/time-series/cluster-robust modelling and explicit effective sample size.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Match the unit of evidence and correlation model to the unit of action; disclose residual dependence.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Fixed subgroup sizes or an X-bar/R worksheet are implementation choices, not the property.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Dependence can be difficult to estimate with few clusters or changing correlation; conservative bounds may be preferable to elaborate fitted models.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should evidence be discounted when shared prompts, seeds, fixtures or upstream data create partially known dependence?

VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.DECISION_PROBLEM: Set limits/uncertainty at the correct process and intervention unit.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.ASSUMED_DATA_GENERATING_PROCESS: Nested/clustered/time-correlated observations with within- and between-group variation.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Identifiers for cluster, order, batch, seed, operator and repeated measurement.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.SIGNAL_OR_DISCRIMINATOR: Between/within decomposition or dependence-adjusted statistic.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_POSITIVE_COST: False alarms or apparent significance from underestimated variance.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_NEGATIVE_COST: Hidden shifts if inappropriate averaging dilutes between-group change.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.NONSTATIONARITY_RISK: Correlation structure itself can drift.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.INTERVENTION_RISK: Adjusting individual readings when the actionable cause is batch/system-level.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Use cluster summaries or conservative effective sample size when modelling is not worth the cost.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Rational grouping or explicit hierarchical/time-series analysis tied to action.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: What is the independent experimental/process unit?
Are repeated same-seed, same-batch or same-evaluator observations being counted as independent?
Do subgroup boundaries correspond to plausible variation mechanisms?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Keep statistical control limits separate from engineering specifications and tolerances
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Shewhart control charts, engineering tolerancing and metrological conformity assessment.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Control limits describe expected process behaviour; specifications define required/allowed performance.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A process can be stable yet unacceptable, or unstable while all observed outputs remain inside specification.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: False assurance, inappropriate alarms and using customer limits as if statistically calibrated.
properties.MECHANISM: Maintain separate provenance and semantics for natural-process limits, specification/tolerance limits and uncertainty/guard bands.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any monitored characteristic with both process history and an external requirement.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For an exact deterministic requirement checked once, a control chart may be unnecessary; use the specification directly with measurement uncertainty.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Authoritative specification, stable-enough process baseline, adequate measurement and explicit conformance decision rule.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Uncertainty near specifications is quantified; specification source/version is fixed.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Control-limit estimation reflects the intended baseline; specs are independent of recent sample behaviour.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents stable bad processes from being celebrated and ordinary variation from being called nonconformance.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Process owner, design authority, customer/regulator and conformance decision maker.
