properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Maintaining multiple limit systems can confuse operators if semantics are not made visible.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Conflation can miss capability problems or create unnecessary intervention.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Setting control limits equal to specs; widening limits to keep data “in control”; treating any in-spec point as evidence of stability.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Three-sigma conventions are not tolerances, and neither system identifies root cause.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward explicit uncertainty-aware conformity rules and capability conditional on stability.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use control limits for change detection, specifications for requirements, and guard bands/decision rules for uncertain conformance.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: One dashboard may display all limits, but their meanings must not be merged.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Specifications themselves may be poorly justified or gamed; statistical separation does not validate the requirement.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should dynamic/adaptive specifications be governed without turning every threshold movement into process redefinition?

VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.DECISION_PROBLEM: Separate detection of process change from conformance to an external requirement.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.ASSUMED_DATA_GENERATING_PROCESS: Process distribution over time plus independent specification boundaries.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Stable measurement scale and uncertainty near boundaries.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.SIGNAL_OR_DISCRIMINATOR: Control signal for change; guard-banded result for conformance.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_POSITIVE_COST: Investigating common variation or rejecting conforming output.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_NEGATIVE_COST: Failing to improve a stable but incapable process.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.NONSTATIONARITY_RISK: Specs or process regimes may change and require separately versioned baselines.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.INTERVENTION_RISK: Widening either limit after failure can erase evidence.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Direct deterministic spec check where monitoring adds no decision value.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Semantically separate control, specification and uncertainty decision rules.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Are requirements/specifications being confused with statistical control limits?
Could the process be stable but incapable, or unstable but currently in specification?
Is measurement uncertainty included in conformance decisions?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Establish process stability before interpreting capability or long-run prediction
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Shewhart statistical control, process characterisation and modern capability standards.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Assess whether the process exhibits sufficiently consistent behaviour before summarising its capability against specifications.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A single capability index can average multiple regimes, trends or special causes into a misleading number.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Predicting future conformance from an unstable historical mixture.
properties.MECHANISM: Use time order, change/mixture checks and process knowledge; if unstable, model regimes or improve/contain before issuing a capability claim.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Capability, tolerance yield, long-run defect rate or predictive performance claims.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a deterministic design proof or 100% authoritative inspection, a statistical capability index may be irrelevant.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Adequate measurement, chronological data, stable specification and enough observations across normal operating conditions.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Evaluator/measurement process is itself stable and capable enough to observe process change.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Future conditions reasonably resemble the characterised regime or are explicitly modelled.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents false long-run assurance and directs improvement toward instability first.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Process/design owner, supplier/customer and regulator.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Demanding global stationarity can block useful local/conditional capability estimates in adaptive or seasonal processes.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Skipping stability can make a high Cpk pure arithmetic over incompatible data.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Shuffled data; pooled shifts/products; one favourable window; rebaselined outliers; no evaluator-stability check.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Finite data cannot prove permanent stability; “stable enough for this prediction horizon” is the mature claim.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from a binary in/out-of-control prerequisite to local, conditional and time-dependent capability models.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: State the regime and prediction horizon; no unconditional capability claim from unresolved drift/mixture.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A mandatory chart is not necessary if equivalent stability evidence exists; the prerequisite is evidential.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Some systems are intentionally nonstationary; capability may need scenario/conditional performance rather than a single process distribution.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What constitutes adequate local stability for adaptive systems with planned policy changes?

VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.DECISION_PROBLEM: Decide whether historical output supports future capability prediction.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.ASSUMED_DATA_GENERATING_PROCESS: A stable or explicitly regime-indexed process distribution.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Chronological, comparable measurements and stable evaluator.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.SIGNAL_OR_DISCRIMINATOR: No material unresolved shifts/mixtures for the stated horizon, or a validated dynamic model.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_POSITIVE_COST: Delaying a useful conditional claim through excessive stationarity demands.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_NEGATIVE_COST: False long-run conformance assurance from unstable pooled data.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.NONSTATIONARITY_RISK: Central risk; local stability may expire.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.INTERVENTION_RISK: Rebaselining can convert instability into apparent capability.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Use conditional descriptive yield without predictive claim.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Capability explicitly conditional on regime, horizon and measurement fitness.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Was stability assessed in time order before capability was reported?
Does the capability number pool distinct products, regimes, populations or evaluator versions?
What prediction horizon and operating conditions does the claim cover?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Use capability indices only conditionally on stability, distribution and measurement fitness
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Process capability analysis, normal-theory indices and ISO 22514 evolution.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Compare process location/spread with specification width using indices such as Cp/Cpk under stated conditions.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A convenient scalar can hide skew, tails, drift, measurement error, centring and subgroup structure.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Sigma-score theatre, unsupported defect-rate conversion and supplier ranking on invalid indices.
properties.MECHANISM: Verify prerequisites; report distribution-free/empirical or model-based alternatives and uncertainty; keep indices subordinate to raw/time-ordered evidence.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: High-volume repeatable processes where a stable distribution and specification-based decision exist.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Use direct yield/tolerance evidence, deterministic limits, or scenario-specific performance when assumptions fail or sample is tiny.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: P018 stability, P002 measurement fitness, representative independent data, stable specification and an adequate distribution/tail model.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Measurement variation is small or incorporated; rounding/censoring do not dominate.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Selected index/distribution describes the regime and tail behaviour; sample size supports intended precision.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Compactly communicates margin and can prioritise centring/variation reduction when valid.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Process engineer, supplier/customer and quality planner.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Index targets encourage gaming, overinvestment and false equivalence among different risk profiles.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Avoiding indices entirely can lose a useful summary when prerequisites genuinely hold.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Cpk on unstable data; normal DPMO conversion under skew/dependence; ignoring confidence intervals; choosing the most favourable index.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Cpk on unstable data; normal DPMO conversion under skew/dependence; ignoring confidence intervals; choosing the most favourable index. Contrary evidence/limit: Tail defect-rate claims can be dominated by model error far beyond observed data; index precision is not tail certainty.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: NIST and ISO narrow capability to stable/in-control or time-dependent models; modern practice reports conditions and uncertainty.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A conditional summary—not evidence of control, causality or universal “sigma level.”
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The index and threshold are optional tools; margin/yield evidence under valid assumptions is the property.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Tail defect-rate claims can be dominated by model error far beyond observed data; index precision is not tail certainty.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: When should capability be expressed as scenario-specific prediction intervals rather than a scalar index?

VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.DECISION_PROBLEM: Summarise whether a stable process can meet specifications.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.ASSUMED_DATA_GENERATING_PROCESS: Stable/regime-specific distribution with known specification limits.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Adequate resolution, low enough measurement error and representative samples.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.SIGNAL_OR_DISCRIMINATOR: Estimated margin/yield with uncertainty under an adequate model.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_POSITIVE_COST: Gaming a scalar target or rejecting acceptable conditional performance.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_NEGATIVE_COST: False assurance in tails or under drift.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.NONSTATIONARITY_RISK: Invalidates static indices unless modelled.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.INTERVENTION_RISK: Changing limits/specs or excluding tails to improve index.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Direct empirical yield/margin or deterministic tolerance analysis.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Conditional index with raw plots, uncertainty and assumption checks.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Are capability prerequisites—stability, measurement fitness and distribution—demonstrated?
Is a sigma/DPMO conversion extrapolating far beyond observed data?
Would direct yield or deterministic margin communicate the decision more honestly?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Prevent tampering and overadjustment to routine variation
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Shewhart economic control and Deming’s later funnel/tampering translation.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Do not alter a stable process in response to fluctuations lacking evidence of an actionable change.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Feedback to noise adds variance, oscillation, bias and instability.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Operator blame, parameter chasing, endless threshold tuning and regression-to-the-mean misread as improvement.
properties.MECHANISM: Define when adjustment is authorised, use calibrated signals/mechanism evidence, and evaluate interventions against a stable baseline or experiment.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Feedback-controlled processes, manual tuning, metric dashboards, repeated reviews and near-threshold variation.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Correct an authoritative deterministic defect immediately; no statistical wait is needed when mechanism/effect is known.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Measurement fitness, action rule, process response knowledge, and ability to distinguish intervention from observation noise.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: The metric is stable enough that an adjustment response is not triggered by evaluator noise.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Unadjusted process has a meaningful baseline and feedback dynamics are understood enough to avoid instability.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces self-inflicted variation, wasted work and false learning.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Operator, process owner and change authority.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Rules too conservative can delay response to small but costly drift.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Rules too permissive create chronic oscillation and hide systemic causes.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Changing settings after every bad point; rewarding short regression-to-mean; retuning evaluator after candidate failure; local optimisation.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: “Do not tamper” must not become “never improve”; designed experiments deliberately change a process under controlled learning.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved into explicit feedback design, intervention analysis and separation of monitoring from experimentation.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: No reactive adjustment without a discriminator or planned experiment whose expected value exceeds intervention risk.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A fixed run rule is not the property; disciplined response to evidence is.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: In rapidly drifting environments, delayed adaptation can be worse than overadjustment; adaptive control must model that trade-off.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should tampering risk be balanced against concept drift when the optimal policy is itself nonstationary?

VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.DECISION_PROBLEM: Decide whether to adjust a process after an observation.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.ASSUMED_DATA_GENERATING_PROCESS: Stable process plus feedback response to interventions, possibly with drift.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Reliable time-ordered metric and known action latency.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.SIGNAL_OR_DISCRIMINATOR: Calibrated signal or mechanism evidence beyond routine variation.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_POSITIVE_COST: Adjustment-induced variance, oscillation and wasted investigation.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_NEGATIVE_COST: Delayed response to real deterioration.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.NONSTATIONARITY_RISK: Changes optimal sensitivity and action cadence.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.INTERVENTION_RISK: Core risk: feedback to noise destabilises the process.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Direct correction for a known deterministic defect.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Predefined response rules plus post-intervention evaluation.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Does the target system change the candidate/process because of noise rather than a discriminating signal?
Could regression to the mean explain the apparent improvement after intervention?
Is the intervention a controlled experiment or untracked parameter chasing?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Design monitoring economically around false-alarm, missed-shift and delay costs
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Shewhart economic control, Duncan economic chart design, CUSUM/EWMA operating characteristics and decision analysis.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Choose sampling frequency, statistic and threshold according to consequential shifts and error/delay costs.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: More sensitive rules can flood operators; conservative rules can miss costly small shifts.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Run-rule ritual, alert fatigue, hidden detection delay and sampling costs exceeding prevention value.
properties.MECHANISM: Define target changes, in-control/out-of-control models or simulations, ARL/delay/precision and consequence-weighted action costs.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Ongoing monitoring with repeated opportunities, finite response capacity and quantifiable consequences.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For rare high-consequence events with a deterministic safety interlock, use the interlock; for low-cost obvious defects, direct inspection may dominate statistical detection.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Actionable response plan, baseline, measurement capability, realistic shift scenarios and cost/risk owner.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Sampling/measurement burden and false-alarm mechanisms are known; alerts can be investigated.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Operating-characteristic calculations approximate real dependence/nonstationarity and cost model includes tail consequences.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Concentrates measurement where it changes decisions and reduces both delay and alert fatigue.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Monitoring designer, operator and risk/economic decision owner.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Monetised cost models may undervalue safety, trust or irreversible loss; overfitting thresholds to history can fail under shift.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Ignoring trade-offs makes “more rules” look unconditionally safer.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Stacking Western Electric rules without capacity; tuning on known incidents; no alert disposition; sampling quota detached from value.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Economic design is powerful but assumption-sensitive and must incorporate non-economic constraints where relevant.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from fixed three-sigma practice to target-shift optimisation, simulations, Bayesian/decision rules and service-capacity-aware alerting.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Select the smallest monitoring design that detects decision-relevant change at acceptable false-alarm/delay cost.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Three sigma, eight run rules or a dashboard cadence are not universal properties.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Cost and shift distributions are often uncertain; robust/minimax or scenario designs may be more honest than a single optimum.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should monitoring be tuned when missed rare events have poorly quantifiable catastrophic loss?

VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.DECISION_PROBLEM: Choose monitoring cadence/statistic/threshold.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.ASSUMED_DATA_GENERATING_PROCESS: Baseline and specified change scenarios with repeated sampling.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Stable measurement and estimated sampling/response costs.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.SIGNAL_OR_DISCRIMINATOR: Operating-characteristic or simulated detection performance.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_POSITIVE_COST: Alert load, investigation cost and tampering.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_NEGATIVE_COST: Damage accumulated before detection.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.NONSTATIONARITY_RISK: Can invalidate expected ARL/delay and cost optimum.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.INTERVENTION_RISK: Rules tuned after incidents can overfit and trigger churn.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Manual periodic review or deterministic interlock for obvious/high-consequence states.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Scenario-robust, capacity-aware monitoring with explicit error costs.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: What shift is the monitor designed to detect, with what delay and false-alarm burden?
Can the organisation investigate the alerts generated by added run rules?
Does another measurement have positive expected decision value?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Adapt monitoring to autocorrelation, seasonality, drift and nonstationarity
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Time-series SPC, residual charts, dynamic models, change-point methods and updated time-dependent capability standards.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Replace naive iid chart assumptions with a model or discriminator appropriate to temporal structure and evolving regimes.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Serial dependence changes false-alarm/detection properties; trends and seasonality can look like special causes or mask them.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: False alarms, missed shifts, invalid limits and rebaselining every natural cycle.
properties.MECHANISM: Model/stratify predictable structure, monitor residuals/forecast errors or use robust change-point methods; validate under simulation/backtests and maintain drift governance.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Metrics with temporal dependence, seasonality, learning curves, policy changes or concept drift.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A large deterministic discontinuity can be handled directly; sparse heterogeneous events may need case-based analysis rather than fitted time series.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Enough history/regimes, stable measurement versions, time metadata, intervention records and a prediction/action horizon.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Evaluator/context changes are versioned; missingness and changing exposure denominators are handled.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Dynamic model/residuals capture enough structure; change-point method’s calibration approximates deployment.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Retains monitoring value while reducing spurious alarms in dynamic systems.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Process owner, forecasting/monitoring team and policy controller.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Complex residual models can whiten away meaningful shifts, overfit history or become unauditable.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Naive static limits can become permanently alarmed or falsely calm.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Fitting seasonality after every alarm; residuals with hidden model failure; changing mixtures; no intervention annotation.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: No universal evolved chart exists; classical methods are narrowed, not simply replaced.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from stationary Shewhart limits to local/regime-aware monitoring, forecast residuals, CUSUM/EWMA and online change detection.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use a transparent dynamic baseline with validated detection properties and explicit rebaseline/change-control rules.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: “Use an AI anomaly detector” is not the property; calibrated discrimination and interpretable response remain required.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Under adversarial or abrupt concept change, historical calibration may fail exactly when needed; guarantees are local/conditional.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can drift detectors distinguish benign adaptation, population change, evaluator change and harmful process degradation?

VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.DECISION_PROBLEM: Detect harmful change in a temporally structured process.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.ASSUMED_DATA_GENERATING_PROCESS: Autocorrelated/seasonal/regime-switching process with interventions.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Stable timestamped measurement and denominator/context metadata.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.SIGNAL_OR_DISCRIMINATOR: Forecast residual, change-point score or regime-conditioned statistic with calibrated delay/error.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_POSITIVE_COST: Persistent spurious alerts and overfitting.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_NEGATIVE_COST: Slow or model-conforming degradation missed.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.NONSTATIONARITY_RISK: Defining feature; calibration expires under unmodelled shifts.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.INTERVENTION_RISK: Rebaselining or model refit may erase incidents.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Stratify by obvious season/regime or use a deterministic event rule.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Validated local/dynamic monitor plus independent model-drift checks.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Are iid/stationarity assumptions plausible for the monitored sequence?
Has seasonality or policy change been modelled rather than called a defect?
Could residual modelling be hiding a materially changed mechanism?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Stratify mixtures, high-mix/low-volume and changing populations before aggregation
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Rational subgrouping, stratification, short-run SPC and mixture-distribution criticism.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Do not pool unlike products, contexts, users or opportunity structures unless the aggregate answers the decision.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Composition change can create or hide trends even when every component is unchanged.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Simpson-type reversals, impossible common limits, false capability and aggregate metric gaming.
properties.MECHANISM: Define comparable strata or standardise/model mix; use short-run/standardised charts only with justified transformations and preserve component views.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: High-mix low-volume production, heterogeneous workloads, changing severity/population or sparse per-type data.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: If all units share the same decision distribution and mixture is stable/irrelevant, aggregate monitoring may be the cheapest valid path.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Product/context identifiers, enough data or engineering standards for normalisation, and a clear aggregate decision.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Measurement is invariant or separately calibrated across strata.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Within-stratum models or standardisation preserve relevant tail/interaction behaviour; no hidden confounding remains.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents composition effects from being attributed to process performance.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Portfolio/process owner and consumers of aggregate dashboards.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Over-stratification produces tiny samples, multiplicity and paralysis; arbitrary normalisation can hide absolute harm.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Under-stratification misses local defects and unfairly rewards favourable mix.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Dropping hard categories; changing denominator; z-scoring incomparable tails; one global control limit; post-hoc subgroup hunting.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Short-run charts help but are domain-specific and assumption-sensitive; hierarchical pooling may be preferable.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from physical product family grouping to hierarchical/partial-pooling and mix-adjusted monitoring.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Show both relevant strata and an explicitly weighted aggregate; freeze/justify weighting and monitor composition.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A mandatory chart per SKU or one universal standardised score are both ceremonial extremes.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: With very sparse strata, estimates depend strongly on hierarchical priors/model sharing; no purely data-driven partition is definitive.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should partial pooling be governed when local safety tails matter more than overall efficiency?

VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.DECISION_PROBLEM: Detect change without confusing it with mixture/composition change.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.ASSUMED_DATA_GENERATING_PROCESS: Mixture of heterogeneous strata with possibly changing weights.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Stratum identity, invariant measurement and denominators.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.SIGNAL_OR_DISCRIMINATOR: Within-stratum or mix-standardised change plus composition monitor.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_POSITIVE_COST: Multiple alerts and false subgroup discoveries.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_NEGATIVE_COST: Local degradation hidden by favourable mix.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.NONSTATIONARITY_RISK: Mixture weights and strata can evolve.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.INTERVENTION_RISK: Changing weights/exclusions can manufacture improvement.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Monitor the dominant/high-risk strata and a transparent aggregate.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Hierarchical or stratified monitoring with fixed/justified weights.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Could a changed product/user/case mix explain the aggregate trend?
Are hard strata being excluded or down-weighted after failures?
Does standardisation preserve the absolute engineering requirement?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Use context-adapted multivariate, rare-event, short-run or change-point monitoring only when its added discrimination pays
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: CUSUM/EWMA, multivariate SPC, attribute/rare-event charts, short-run methods and modern change detection.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Choose a monitoring statistic matched to event type, dimension, baseline size and target change rather than force a classical chart.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Univariate normal charts can miss joint shifts, mis-handle sparse events, or be unusable with one-off/high-mix output.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Tool mismatch, multiplicity across dashboards, tail overconfidence and opaque anomaly scores.
properties.MECHANISM: Specify the change/event to detect, compare candidate methods by simulated/empirical operating characteristics, and keep a causal/actionable interpretation.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Multivariate correlated measurements, rare defects, variable exposure, small shifts, low volume or abrupt change points.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Use a direct rule or simple stratified count when the event is obvious and data too sparse to estimate a complex model.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable measurement, exposure denominators, enough baseline or engineering prior, response plan and computational/interpretive capacity.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Input variables retain meaning and covariance/event models are adequate enough for threshold calibration.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Selected detector’s null/change model or robust calibration approximates use; multiplicity across monitored features is controlled.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Improves sensitivity where classical charts are structurally mismatched.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Monitoring team and incident/process owner.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Complex detectors create opaque false alarms, overfit baselines and encourage dashboard proliferation.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Simple charts can miss joint/slow/rare changes with serious consequences.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Hotelling score without diagnosis; Poisson chart under overdispersion; zero-event reassurance; model retrained after every alarm.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Hotelling score without diagnosis; Poisson chart under overdispersion; zero-event reassurance; model retrained after every alarm. Contrary evidence/limit: Rare-event detector performance is often weakly estimable; simulation depends on an assumed tail/model and can create false certainty.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Extensions retain the underlying discrimination property but remain domain/model-specific.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Adopt only after showing incremental decision value over a cheap baseline, with interpretable follow-up and recalibration rules.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Having a multivariate/anomaly model is not a general property; validated added discrimination is.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Rare-event detector performance is often weakly estimable; simulation depends on an assumed tail/model and can create false certainty.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What evidence threshold is sufficient to deploy a complex detector when incidents are too rare for direct validation?

VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.DECISION_PROBLEM: Select a detector for multivariate, sparse, small-shift or low-volume change.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.ASSUMED_DATA_GENERATING_PROCESS: Context-specific joint/event/regime model, often with limited baseline data.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Stable features, denominators, covariance/event definitions and protected calibration data.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.SIGNAL_OR_DISCRIMINATOR: Detector score calibrated to target change and error costs.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_POSITIVE_COST: Opaque alert burden, multiple-testing inflation and overfit.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_NEGATIVE_COST: Joint/rare harmful shift missed by simple marginal rules.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.NONSTATIONARITY_RISK: Model/calibration particularly fragile under shift.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.INTERVENTION_RISK: Retraining after incidents can absorb failures.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Direct count/rule or expert review when data cannot support a complex detector.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Incremental-value-tested specialised monitor with interpretable diagnosis.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: What specific change does the specialised detector find that a cheaper rule misses?
Are rare-event or covariance assumptions supported?
Can an alert be translated into an actionable investigation rather than an opaque score?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Design sampling to represent the decision population and selection process
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Probability sampling, industrial inspection, survey/experimental design and modern dataset-shift analysis.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Define the target population/opportunity frame and select units so inclusion supports the intended inference.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A large convenient sample can be systematically unrepresentative, duplicated or selected after outcomes are visible.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Selection bias, survivorship bias, spectrum restriction and false precision from nonprobability coverage.
properties.MECHANISM: Specify frame, inclusion probabilities or explicit selection model; stratify high-risk/rare groups; document exclusions and compare sample to target.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any inference beyond the exactly observed units, especially acceptance, prevalence, reliability or benchmark claims.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For exhaustive authoritative enumeration of the entire relevant population, statistical sampling is unnecessary; verify completeness/identity instead.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Defined target population, unit/opportunity, frame coverage, provenance and a plan for nonresponse/missingness.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Measurement meaning is invariant enough across sampled and target contexts; duplicates and clusters are identified.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Probability or selection-model assumptions hold sufficiently; unobserved selection is bounded or disclosed.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Makes uncertainty and transfer claims correspond to the population that drives the decision.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Experimenter, quality/reliability analyst, customer/regulator and benchmark consumer.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Complex representative sampling may cost more than direct inspection or targeted risk sampling; strict probability designs may undersample rare hazards.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Convenience samples can miss failure modes no amount of replication recovers.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Public/easy cases only; post-failure exclusion; duplicated source records; favourable time window; target population left implicit.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Probability sampling does not repair invalid measurement, and nonprobability samples can still support bounded local decisions if claims are restricted.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved toward risk-stratified, cluster-aware, importance-weighted and shift-monitored sampling while preserving explicit target definition.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use the cheapest design that either represents the target or honestly limits the claim; retain all attempted-unit provenance.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A sample-size quota without a target/frame is ceremony.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Open-ended deployment populations cannot be fully represented in advance; monitoring and scenario coverage remain necessary.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should rare catastrophic strata be oversampled while preserving interpretable overall estimates?

EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.HYPOTHESIS_OR_DECISION: Estimate or compare performance for a defined target population.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPERIMENTAL_UNIT: Independently sampled unit or explicitly clustered unit from the frame.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INDEPENDENCE_ASSUMPTION: Sampling clusters/duplicates and repeated units must be modelled.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.RANDOMISATION_OR_CONTROL: Random selection or transparent risk/stratified design; treatment randomisation is a separate issue.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.BLOCKING_OR_STRATIFICATION: Stratify by expected heterogeneity, rarity or decision loss.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.REPLICATION_MEANING: Replication means new sampled units, not repeated measurement of the same unit.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INTERACTION_RISK: Sample composition can interact with candidate/treatment performance.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.STOPPING_RULE: Pre-specify frame, inclusion/exclusion and replacement rules.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Provides population-relevant uncertainty and exposes coverage gaps.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.COST: Frame construction, oversampling and follow-up.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED: Overengineered probability sampling may waste effort for local deterministic decisions.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Explicit target/frame with representative or claim-limited sampling.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: What exact population and opportunity frame does the sample represent?
Could selection, survival or duplication explain the result?
Would exhaustive deterministic checking be cheaper or more authoritative?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Use acceptance sampling only for bounded lot-disposition decisions where inspection cost or destruction justifies it
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Dodge–Romig Bell Labs sampling inspection, wartime/industrial standards and current ISO 2859.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Accept or reject a lot using a prespecified sampling plan with producer/consumer operating risks.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: 100% inspection may be destructive, too slow, too expensive or itself error-prone.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Arbitrary lot release, hidden risk transfer and pretending a sample proves every item conforms.
properties.MECHANISM: Choose plan by lot structure, AQL/LQ or OC requirements, inspection error and cost; preserve switching/traceability and disposition semantics.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Incoming/outgoing lots with meaningful lot identity, relatively stable supply and costly/destructive inspection.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Use 100% deterministic inspection when cheap/reliable; use process control/improvement when the goal is future quality rather than one-lot disposition.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Defined lot, random sample, valid attribute/variable measurement, prespecified plan and clear producer/consumer risk.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Inspection error is small or included; sample selection cannot be manipulated.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Within-lot heterogeneity and production history are compatible with the plan; standard’s switching rules/context apply.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Controls transaction risk at lower inspection cost and limits destructive sampling.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Purchaser/supplier, release authority and regulator.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: A sampling plan can accept bad items/lots by design and may institutionalise tolerable defects or adversarial lot formation.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Overly small/lenient plans expose consumers to unacceptable lots.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: AQL interpreted as a guarantee; nonrandom sample; lot splitting; plan chosen after results; inspection error ignored.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: AQL interpreted as a guarantee; nonrandom sample; lot splitting; plan chosen after results; inspection error ignored. Contrary evidence/limit: Changing lot composition, adversarial suppliers and severe item heterogeneity can invalidate nominal OC risks.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Modern standards retain the tool but explicitly limit it to acceptance decisions, not process estimation or prevention.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A domain-specific decision procedure with transparent OC/risk—not a universal quality property.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: ISO table use or a named MIL-STD plan is an implementation; bounded risk-based lot disposition is the property.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Changing lot composition, adversarial suppliers and severe item heterogeneity can invalidate nominal OC risks.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: When do modern automated inspections make classical sampling economically obsolete?

VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.DECISION_PROBLEM: Accept/reject a finite lot under inspection cost and error risk.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.ASSUMED_DATA_GENERATING_PROCESS: Finite lot with random sampled items and specified defect model/OC curve.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Reliable item classification and auditable random sample.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.SIGNAL_OR_DISCRIMINATOR: Acceptance number/plan with stated producer and consumer risks.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_POSITIVE_COST: Rejecting good lot, delay and destructive cost.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.FALSE_NEGATIVE_COST: Accepting bad lot or catastrophic defective item.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.NONSTATIONARITY_RISK: Lot heterogeneity/formation changes nominal risks.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.INTERVENTION_RISK: Switching or relabelling lots after failure can game the plan.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: 100% reliable automated inspection or direct supplier process evidence.
VARIATION_CONTROL_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Prespecified OC-based plan restricted to lot disposition.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Is the decision one-lot disposition, rather than process improvement or a universal quality claim?
Are sample selection, lot identity and inspection error controlled?
Would 100% authoritative inspection now be cheaper or safer?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Do not use acceptance sampling as a substitute for process understanding, prevention or improvement
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Limits recognised in acceptance-sampling handbooks and the shift from end inspection toward process control/prevention.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Separate transaction screening from evidence about why a process generates defects and how future output will behave.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Passing lots can coexist with a poor, drifting or gamed process; rejected lots do not identify the cause.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Inspection dependence, hidden scrap/rework, no learning and claims that accepted samples establish process capability.
properties.MECHANISM: Pair lot disposition with supplier/process feedback, time-ordered defect analysis, corrective action or designed improvement where economically justified.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Repeated supply/production where future quality matters, not merely one isolated transaction.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a one-off purchase with no leverage or future process, bounded acceptance sampling may be all that is rational.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Lot and process identities linked, defect provenance retained, and process owner able to act.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Measurement system distinguishes defects and records failure modes rather than only pass/fail totals.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Lot outcomes contain some information about process, but causal diagnosis requires additional evidence.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Converts inspection cost into learning and prevents sampling plans from becoming a quality ceiling.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Supplier/process owner, procurement and improvement team.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Demanding improvement evidence can be uneconomic for commodity/one-off purchases.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Pure screening leaves recurrent systemic defects untouched.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Discarding rejected-lot data; treating AQL as target; supplier adjusts lot formation; no root-cause evidence.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Discarding rejected-lot data; treating AQL as target; supplier adjusts lot formation; no root-cause evidence. Contrary evidence/limit: For highly regulated or destructive products, acceptance evidence may remain necessary even with excellent process control.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: The evolved form retains acceptance sampling only as one control layer, subordinated to prevention and feedback.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use sampling for the decision it can make; do not infer control, capability or cause from acceptance alone.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Acceptance forms/tables are not process-improvement properties.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: For highly regulated or destructive products, acceptance evidence may remain necessary even with excellent process control.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What combination of process evidence and lot inspection minimises total risk under supplier/adversarial uncertainty?
QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Is lot acceptance being mistaken for evidence of process stability or cause?
Are rejected and sampled defects fed back into process learning?
Is future process improvement economically relevant to this decision?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Size samples around effect/precision, dependence and decision loss—not a universal count
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Neyman–Pearson power, estimation precision, sampling theory, cluster design and reliability bounds.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Choose information volume from the smallest meaningful effect or required precision, error costs, variance, design and stopping plan.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Too few independent units miss meaningful effects; many dependent or biased units create only false precision.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Underpowered/equivocal experiments, inflated cost, post-hoc stopping and “large n” used to excuse bad design.
properties.MECHANISM: Specify decision margin, alpha/beta or interval width/utility, estimate design effects, use simulation/sensitivity, and distinguish units from repeated measurements.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Sampling/experiment/reliability decisions where uncertainty influences action.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: No sample-size calculation is needed when a deterministic proof/check resolves the decision or when a pilot’s only goal is feasibility discovery.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Defined estimand/decision, plausible variance/effect range, independent-unit structure, multiplicity/stopping plan and feasible measurement.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Measurement error and missingness are included in effective information; pilot estimates are not treated as exact.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Planning model approximates design; effect threshold is engineering-justified; clusters/dependence known enough.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Avoids both information-starved decisions and wasteful quota measurement.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Experiment owner, risk owner and resource allocator.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Rigid power targets can encourage guessed effect sizes, oversized studies for trivial effects, or neglect of catastrophic rare modes.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Small effective n yields unstable estimates and inconclusive negatives.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Counting repeated readings as n; planning on observed pilot effect; stopping when significant; ignoring multiplicity/attrition.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Counting repeated readings as n; planning on observed pilot effect; stopping when significant; ignoring multiplicity/attrition. Contrary evidence/limit: Rare catastrophic outcomes may require physical/structural evidence, conservative bounds or stress models because feasible samples cannot directly validate target rates.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from fixed-horizon power calculations toward precision, simulation, sequential/decision-theoretic and assurance approaches.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Plan for the independent information needed to discriminate the decision, update only under a valid sequential/adaptive protocol.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: “30 samples,” “10 runs,” or “80% power” without a decision model is ceremony.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Rare catastrophic outcomes may require physical/structural evidence, conservative bounds or stress models because feasible samples cannot directly validate target rates.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should sample planning combine epistemic uncertainty in variance/effect with asymmetric catastrophic loss?

EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.HYPOTHESIS_OR_DECISION: Obtain enough independent information to choose among actions or bound risk.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPERIMENTAL_UNIT: Independent experimental/sample unit at the decision scale.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INDEPENDENCE_ASSUMPTION: Clusters, repeated measures and common seeds reduce effective n.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.RANDOMISATION_OR_CONTROL: Assignment/sampling design determines variance and bias; randomisation where causal.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.BLOCKING_OR_STRATIFICATION: Use stratification/blocking when it reduces nuisance variance without hiding heterogeneity.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.REPLICATION_MEANING: New independent units; technical repeats mainly estimate measurement error.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INTERACTION_RISK: Interactions/heterogeneity increase required coverage and can invalidate one average effect.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.STOPPING_RULE: Fixed horizon or formally planned sequential/adaptive rule.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Decision discrimination or interval precision per unit cost.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.COST: Units, measurement, delay and opportunity cost.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED: Formulaic power can become a quota and reward trivial-effect detection.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Simulation/sensitivity-based planning with explicit effect, dependence, loss and stopping.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: What independent sample size—not raw observation count—supports the decision?
What smallest engineering-relevant effect or precision target was used?
Would a sequential or deterministic path reach the decision more cheaply?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Frame experiments around an explicit engineering decision, estimand and rival alternatives
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Fisherian experiment purpose, Neyman–Pearson specified alternatives, causal estimands and statistical engineering.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: State what contrast/effect/population and action the experiment is intended to discriminate before selecting a test.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A technically valid analysis can answer an irrelevant null, average over decisive heterogeneity, or lack an action consequence.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Significance-test ritual, moving hypotheses, post-hoc target selection and experiments that generate numbers but no decision.
properties.MECHANISM: Define decision, estimand, experimental unit, rival explanations, smallest consequential effect, validity scope and stopping/analysis plan.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any nontrivial comparison or intervention whose result may change design, release, allocation or policy.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For an exact authoritative check or exploratory feasibility probe, a formal estimand/test may be unnecessary; label the evidence accordingly.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stakeholder/engineering loss, target population, manipulable treatment/design alternatives and measurable outcome.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Outcome is valid and sensitive enough; unit/assignment/exposure can be identified.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: The chosen estimand maps to the decision and potential outcomes/comparisons are meaningful.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents expensive but non-decisive experimentation and makes negative/ambiguous outcomes interpretable.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Design authority, product/process owner and risk/resource decision maker.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Prematurely narrow estimands can miss discovery or emergent failure modes.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Vague goals permit post-hoc success definitions and false causal stories.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Null of exactly zero; endpoint switched after results; no target population; average effect hides catastrophic subgroup.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: No universal formalism resolves normative loss or construct definition; exploratory and confirmatory phases may differ.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved from hypothesis testing toward explicit estimands, decision margins, rival models and staged exploration/confirmation.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: No experiment begins as “run a test”; it begins with the decision it can change and the cheapest evidence that discriminates it.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A preregistration form or test name is optional; frozen decision/estimand boundaries are the property.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Some engineering discovery is necessarily open-ended; the mature boundary is transparent separation of exploration from decision-confirming evidence.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should multi-objective engineering decisions state estimands without hiding value trade-offs in a scalar?

EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.HYPOTHESIS_OR_DECISION: Choose among stated engineering alternatives using a defined effect/estimand.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPERIMENTAL_UNIT: Unit receiving the intervention/design condition.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INDEPENDENCE_ASSUMPTION: The unit—not each output—is the independent replication basis unless a justified hierarchy is modelled.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.RANDOMISATION_OR_CONTROL: Randomise or justify a controlled quasi-experimental assignment.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.BLOCKING_OR_STRATIFICATION: Block nuisance variation relevant to precision/validity.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.REPLICATION_MEANING: New independently assigned units across decision-relevant conditions.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INTERACTION_RISK: Specify interactions that could reverse the average decision.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.STOPPING_RULE: Fixed or planned sequential rule tied to the estimand.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Expected reduction in uncertainty between rival actions.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.COST: Experiment units, delay, risk and opportunity.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED: Over-formal framing can suppress exploratory learning.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Staged exploratory/confirmatory design with explicit estimand, decision margin and scope.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: What exact decision and rival alternatives will the experiment discriminate?
Is the estimand aligned with the unit/population that will receive the action?
Would a cheaper authoritative observation settle the question?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Use randomisation to protect causal comparisons against assignment bias and support valid error assessment
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Fisher’s field experiments, randomised experiments and potential-outcomes causal inference.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Allocate experimental units by a known chance mechanism so treatment is not systematically confounded with observed/unobserved pre-treatment factors.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Convenient or outcome-informed assignment can make association look causal.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Selection bias, time/order confounding and invalid reference distributions.
properties.MECHANISM: Randomise at the correct unit, conceal/record allocation, account for restrictions/clusters, and analyse according to the actual assignment.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: When interventions are feasible and the causal effect matters.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Randomisation is unnecessary for deterministic mechanism verification and may be infeasible/unethical; strong natural/quasi-experimental or mechanistic evidence can be used with narrower claims.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Defined experimental unit, feasible comparable conditions, stable measurement, compliance/exposure records and enough independent assignments.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Outcome ascertainment is blinded or otherwise protected from allocation bias where possible.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: No unmodelled interference/carryover; randomisation is implemented, not merely planned; attrition does not undo comparability.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Supports causal discrimination and honest uncertainty with fewer modelling assumptions about assignment.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Experimenter, design/process owner and causal decision consumer.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Randomisation can be costly, expose units to inferior conditions, or average over important heterogeneity; chance imbalance remains possible.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Without it, hidden assignment bias may dominate even large samples.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Randomising observations instead of units; deterministic seed reused; allocation predictable; post-randomisation exclusions; interference ignored.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Randomisation does not solve invalid measurement, low power, noncompliance, spillover, external validity or poor estimands.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved into cluster, stratified, covariate-adaptive and online randomisation with transparent assignment logs.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Randomise when it materially reduces causal ambiguity; preserve assignment integrity and analyse the design actually run.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: “A/B test” branding or a random seed alone is not the property.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Randomised effects may not transport beyond sampled units/context, and operational noncompliance can change the estimand.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: When is mechanism-plus-observational evidence decision-sufficient despite infeasible randomisation?

EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.HYPOTHESIS_OR_DECISION: Estimate the causal effect of an intervention/design alternative.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPERIMENTAL_UNIT: Unit assigned to treatment/control.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INDEPENDENCE_ASSUMPTION: Units are independent or clustering/interference is designed and analysed.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.RANDOMISATION_OR_CONTROL: Known recorded random allocation; concealment/blinding where relevant.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.BLOCKING_OR_STRATIFICATION: Restricted/stratified randomisation for major nuisance factors.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.REPLICATION_MEANING: Independent assigned units; repeated outcomes are within-unit data.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INTERACTION_RISK: Treatment effects may vary by block/context; pre-specify important modifiers.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.STOPPING_RULE: Fixed or design-valid sequential boundaries.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Removes assignment confounding in expectation and supports randomisation inference.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.COST: Exposure to alternatives, sample/time and operational disruption.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED: Randomising trivial questions can waste resources or violate safety constraints.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Correct-unit randomisation plus measurement, compliance, interference and transport safeguards.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Was allocation randomised at the actual intervention unit?
Could order, selection, attrition or exposure violate the assignment comparison?
What causal ambiguity remains despite randomisation?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Block or stratify known nuisance variation without erasing interactions
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Fisher’s local control/blocking, factorial design and modern stratified/randomised experiments.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Group or balance experimental units on nuisance factors before randomisation/analysis to reduce unexplained variance and confounding.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Batch, time, operator, hardware, site or baseline severity can obscure or mimic treatment effects.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Low precision, imbalance, order effects and effects confounded with known nuisance structure.
properties.MECHANISM: Select a few consequential pre-treatment factors, block/stratify randomisation and estimate block/treatment interactions when relevant.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Heterogeneous units or expensive experiments where nuisance variation is large relative to target effect.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Do not block on post-treatment variables or add complexity when units are already homogeneous and the effect is obvious.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Known pre-treatment covariates, enough units per block or matched-pair structure, and stable measurement.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Blocking variables are measured before intervention without candidate-induced bias.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Within-block comparisons remain meaningful; block definitions are not chosen after outcomes.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Increases precision and protects comparisons, often reducing required runs.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Experimenter and engineering decision owner.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Too many/tiny blocks reduce degrees of freedom, break randomisation or hide generalisation; bad matching can amplify bias.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: No blocking may leave a cheap major source of variation unaddressed.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Blocking treatment with time unintentionally; post-hoc subgrouping; using seed as “replication” but not block; forgetting block interactions.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Blocking treatment with time unintentionally; post-hoc subgrouping; using seed as “replication” but not block; forgetting block interactions. Contrary evidence/limit: When nuisance variables are numerous/high-dimensional, model-based adjustment may overfit; design-stage balance remains finite.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Modern practice combines blocking with regression/hierarchical adjustment but retains design-stage protection.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Block what is known and costly, randomise what remains, and report context interactions rather than only an adjusted average.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A Latin square or mandatory stratification table is optional; nuisance-control efficiency is the property.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: When nuisance variables are numerous/high-dimensional, model-based adjustment may overfit; design-stage balance remains finite.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which factors merit blocking versus deliberate exploration as potential interactions?

EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.HYPOTHESIS_OR_DECISION: Estimate an effect with reduced nuisance variance and confounding.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPERIMENTAL_UNIT: Unit within a pre-treatment block/stratum.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INDEPENDENCE_ASSUMPTION: Independence across units/blocks or explicit cluster model.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.RANDOMISATION_OR_CONTROL: Randomise within blocks or use justified matched assignment.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.BLOCKING_OR_STRATIFICATION: Core mechanism: predefine blocks on consequential nuisance factors.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.REPLICATION_MEANING: Independent units within/among blocks; technical repeats do not replace units.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INTERACTION_RISK: Treatment×block interactions may limit generalisation.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.STOPPING_RULE: Predefine block construction and stopping.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Higher precision per run and protection from known imbalance.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.COST: Design complexity and need for enough units per block.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED: Overblocking/empty cells and post-hoc stratification.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Sparse, pre-treatment blocking plus interaction-aware analysis.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Were known batch, time, operator, site or severity effects blocked/stratified?
Was any block defined after outcomes or affected by treatment?
Could the treatment effect reverse across blocks?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Require independent replication at the experimental-unit level; treat technical repeats as measurement information
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Fisherian replication, hierarchical experimental design and Hurlbert’s pseudoreplication critique.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Repeat treatments on genuinely independent units so variability relevant to generalisation is observed.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Many outputs, seeds, subsamples or repeated readings from one unit can look like a large experiment while providing one treatment assignment.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Underestimated uncertainty, false significance, fragile “6/6” claims and inability to distinguish unit effects from treatment effects.
properties.MECHANISM: Define unit/cluster, allocate multiple independent units per condition, model nesting/repeated measures and label technical replication explicitly.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any claim intended to generalise beyond one specimen, run, model instance, batch, site or environment.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For deterministic proof or exact exhaustive checks, replication is unnecessary; for measurement precision, technical repeats remain useful but answer a different question.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Multiple independent units, provenance showing common sources, and a stable treatment/evaluator protocol.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Repeated measurement error is separated from between-unit variation; evaluator exposures do not couple units.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Units are exchangeable/representative enough for intended scope; clusters and interference are modelled.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Produces honest uncertainty and tests robustness across naturally varying units.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Experimenter, reviewer and engineering decision authority.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Independent replication can be expensive or impossible for unique systems; demanding it mechanically may block mechanistic evidence.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Pseudo-replication creates arbitrarily narrow intervals without additional independent information.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Same seed/environment; multiple metrics from one run; split observations from one batch; repeated test after adaptation; duplicated data lineage.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Replication count is not enough: independence, representativeness and measurement validity remain prerequisites.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved into multilevel models, cluster-robust inference, multisite replication and explicit technical/biological/system-level replication labels.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Count independent decision-relevant units, disclose dependence, and stop treating correlated reruns as corroboration.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A fixed “number of replications” is ceremony; independence at the right level is the property.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: For singular large engineered systems, evidence may need component replication, simulation validation and mechanistic argument rather than classical independent system copies.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What constitutes independent replication for stochastic software/agent systems sharing training data, code and evaluator?

EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.HYPOTHESIS_OR_DECISION: Generalise a treatment/design effect beyond one realised unit.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPERIMENTAL_UNIT: Independent specimen/run/site/model instance/batch receiving a condition.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INDEPENDENCE_ASSUMPTION: Technical repeats and outputs nested within units are correlated.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.RANDOMISATION_OR_CONTROL: Randomise conditions across independent units when causal.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.BLOCKING_OR_STRATIFICATION: Block by known shared source while retaining multiple units per condition.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.REPLICATION_MEANING: New units with independent exposure and natural variation.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INTERACTION_RISK: Treatment×unit/context interactions reveal transfer limits.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.STOPPING_RULE: Set independent-unit target or valid sequential rule before outcome review.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: Estimates between-unit variability and robustness.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.COST: Independent units may dominate total cost.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED: Mechanical replication quotas or fake seed replication.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Hierarchical design that labels technical, unit, batch and site replication separately.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: What is the actual independently assigned or sampled unit?
Are multiple outputs, seeds or reviews from one underlying unit being counted as separate experiments?
Does shared data, evaluator or environment create common-mode dependence?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Use factorial structure to discover interactions and avoid one-factor-at-a-time ambiguity
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Fisherian factorial designs and industrial DOE.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Vary multiple factors jointly so main effects and interactions can be estimated efficiently.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: One-factor-at-a-time trials miss synergies/antagonisms and can recommend settings that fail in combination.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Confounded design choices, local conclusions and excessive runs for weak information.
properties.MECHANISM: Use full or suitable fractional factorial designs, randomisation/blocking and hierarchy/sparsity only as stated assumptions; confirm consequential interactions.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Multiple controllable factors with plausible interactions and experiments costly enough that structured coverage matters.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For one known dominant factor, deterministic mechanism or a tiny safe search space that can be exhaustively tested, formal factorial DOE may be excessive.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable factor levels, adequate measurement, feasible combinations, enough units, and a response meaningful over the design region.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Outcome/evaluator remains comparable across combinations; invalid/impossible combinations identified before randomisation.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Model hierarchy/sparsity or sufficient full design; no uncontrolled time/batch confounding.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Finds interactions with fewer runs than sequential one-factor searches and improves design robustness.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Design/process engineer and optimiser.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: Factorial grids can explode, include unrealistic combinations, and overfit interaction terms with limited replication.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Ignoring interactions can produce brittle settings and false “best factor” claims.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: OFAT; no randomisation; main effects interpreted despite strong interactions; multiple responses cherry-picked; no confirmation.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Factorial design is not synonymous with all experimentation; interactions outside tested levels/context remain unknown.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Evolved into screening, optimal/computer designs, sequential augmentation and hierarchical modelling.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use factorial structure when interaction ambiguity is decision-relevant; confirm in the intended operating region.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A full 2^k table is optional; efficient interaction-identifying contrast structure is the property.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: High-dimensional systems may violate effect sparsity/hierarchy and contain discontinuities; adaptive or mechanistic designs may outperform classical factorials.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should factor screening incorporate safety constraints and rare catastrophic interactions?

EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.HYPOTHESIS_OR_DECISION: Estimate main effects and interactions among controllable factors.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPERIMENTAL_UNIT: Independent run/unit at a specified factor combination.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INDEPENDENCE_ASSUMPTION: Runs independent or blocked; repeated readings nested.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.RANDOMISATION_OR_CONTROL: Randomise run order subject to safety/logistics.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.BLOCKING_OR_STRATIFICATION: Block batch/day/machine or use split-plot structure when factor changes differ in cost.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.REPLICATION_MEANING: Independent runs across combinations; confirmatory runs at chosen settings.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.INTERACTION_RISK: Core target; hierarchy/sparsity assumptions must be explicit.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.STOPPING_RULE: Preplan analysis and reserve confirmation; sequential augmentation allowed by rule.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.EXPECTED_INFORMATION_GAIN: High information per run about combinations and robustness.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.COST: Number of combinations, setup changes and unsafe regions.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED: Overbuilt factorials and spurious high-order interactions.
EXPERIMENT_DISCRIMINATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Smallest design that identifies decision-relevant interactions plus confirmation.

QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT: Could interactions reverse the conclusion drawn from isolated factor changes?
Is the design able to separate main effects from important interactions?
Would exhaustive/deterministic testing be cheaper than a formal DOE here?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Use fractional factorial/screening designs only with explicit alias and sparsity assumptions
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Plackett–Burman, fractional factorial resolution theory and industrial screening.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Screen many factors with fewer runs by accepting known confounding/alias structure.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A low-resolution design can mistake interactions for main effects or declare inactive factors under false sparsity.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Confident but aliased conclusions, discarded causal factors and optimisation on a contaminated screening model.
properties.MECHANISM: Choose resolution by plausible interactions, inspect alias matrix, randomise/block, use foldover/augmentation or independent confirmation.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Early screening with many candidate factors, limited runs and a credible effect-sparsity/hierarchy hypothesis.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Use full factorial, mechanistic screening or direct elimination when interactions are dense/critical or factors are few.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Known factor ranges, stable measurement, feasible design matrix, predeclared alias tolerance and resources for follow-up.
properties.MEASUREMENT_PRECONDITIONS: Measurement error small enough that sparse effects are not buried; factor settings are reproducible.
properties.ASSUMPTIONS: Few active effects, high-order interactions negligible or follow-up can resolve ambiguity.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces experimental burden while identifying promising factors for later study.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Screening experiment owner and design team.
properties.FALSE_POSITIVE_OR_OVERREACTION_RISK: False economy if follow-up is omitted; alias assumptions can be chosen after results to tell a preferred story.
properties.FALSE_NEGATIVE_OR_MISSED_SIGNAL_RISK: Avoiding screening may make broad factor exploration infeasible.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Resolution III main effects treated as clean; no foldover; factors dropped before interaction check; no confirmation.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The property is bounded by its stated assumptions and known failures: Resolution III main effects treated as clean; no foldover; factors dropped before interaction check; no confirmation. Contrary evidence/limit: When effect sparsity fails or factors are adaptive/continuous, screening rankings can be unstable and model-dependent.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Modern practice uses sequential augmentation, Bayesian/sparsity models and optimal designs but cannot eliminate aliasing without information.
